tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

    def _watch_worker(self, proc: subprocess.Popen) -> None:
        while proc.poll() is None:
            if self.stop_ev.is_set():
                kill_tree(proc.pid)
                return
            touch_lock(self.p["lock"])
            time.sleep(2)

    # ---- loops
    def settle(self, cfg: dict, wait: float = 2.0) -> None:
        """For `once`: two samples apart; files whose size did not change are treated as stable (mtime still has
        to be older than stable_s)."""
        with _state_lock:
            st = self._load()
            self.rescan(cfg, st)
            self._save(st)
        time.sleep(wait)
        with _state_lock:
            st = self._load()
            now = time.time()
            before = {k: (v["size"], v["mtime"]) for k, v in st["files"].items()}
            self.rescan(cfg, st, now)
            for k, v in st["files"].items():
                if before.get(k) == (v["size"], v["mtime"]):
                    self.tracker.prime(k)
            self._save(st)

    def once(self, ignore_game: bool = False, force_enabled: bool = True) -> list[str]:
        """Process everything that is ready now; returns the tick results."""
        cfg = self.cfg()
        self.settle({**cfg, "wait_for_game": False})
        out = []
        while not self.stop_ev.is_set():
            r = self.tick(force=force_enabled, ignore_game=ignore_game)
            out.append(r)
            if r != "processed":
                break
        release_lock(self.p["lock"])
        return out

    def run_forever(self, stop: threading.Event | None = None) -> None:
        if stop is not None:
            self.stop_ev = stop
        self.log("started")
        try:
            while not self.stop_ev.is_set():
                kicked = False
                if self.p["kick"].exists():
                    try:
                        self.p["kick"].unlink()
                    except OSError:
                        pass
                    kicked = True
                try:
                    r = self.tick(force=kicked, ignore_game=kicked)
                except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - never crash the loop
                    self.log(f"tick error: {type(ex).__name__}: {ex}")
                    r = "error"
                if r == "off":
                    release_lock(self.p["lock"])
                nap = 1.0 if r == "processed" else float(self.cfg()["poll_s"])
                t_end = time.time() + nap
                while time.time() < t_end and not self.stop_ev.is_set() and not self.p["kick"].exists():
                    self.stop_ev.wait(1.0)
        finally:
            if self.proc:
                kill_tree(self.proc.pid)
            release_lock(self.p["lock"])
            self.set_status("stopped", "Autopilot stopped.")

    def request_stop(self) -> None:
        self.stop_ev.set()
        if self.proc:
            kill_tree(self.proc.pid)


def kill_tree(pid: int) -> None:
    _hidden(["taskkill", "/F", "/T", "/PID", str(pid)], 15)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ background thread for the UI server
_bg: Autopilot | None = None
_bg_thread: threading.Thread | None = None


def start_background() -> None:
    """Called by the studio server: a daemon thread that idles while autopilot.enabled is off and works when it is on.
    A CLI instance holding the lock makes this one stand down (the lock has a PID + heartbeat)."""
    global _bg, _bg_thread
    if _bg_thread and _bg_thread.is_alive():
        return
    _bg = Autopilot()
    _bg_thread = threading.Thread(target=_bg.run_forever, name="autopilot", daemon=True)
    _bg_thread.start()
    atexit.register(stop_background)


def stop_background() -> None:
    if _bg:
        _bg.request_stop()
    if _bg_thread:
        _bg_thread.join(timeout=8)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ API used by the server / CLI
def api_state(state_path: Path | None = None, limit: int = 40) -> dict:
    p = paths_for(state_path)
    cfg = load_config()
    st = load_state(p["state"])
    status = _read_json(p["status"], {}) or {}
    holder = lock_holder(p["lock"])
    alive = holder is not None
    if not alive and status.get("state") not in (None, "stopped"):
        status = {**status, "state": "stopped", "message": "Autopilot is not running."}
    runs = sorted(st["files"].values(), key=lambda e: e.get("finished") or e.get("started") or e.get("first_seen") or 0,
                  reverse=True)[:limit]
    counts: dict = {}
    for e in st["files"].values():
        counts[e["status"]] = counts.get(e["status"], 0) + 1
    if not cfg["enabled"] and not (alive and status.get("state") == "processing"):
        status = {"state": "off", "message": "Autopilot is off. Turn it on and play: your video will appear by itself."}
    elif cfg["enabled"] and not alive:
        status = {"state": "stopped", "message": "Autopilot is on, but nothing is running it yet (it starts with the "
                  "studio UI, or run: uv run mcs autopilot run)."}
    return {"config": {k: cfg[k] for k in ("enabled", "watch_folders", "output_folder", "min_length_s", "max_age_h",
                                           "wait_for_game", "make_shorts", "render_final")},
            "status": status, "alive": alive, "pid": holder, "counts": counts, "runs": runs}


def kick(state_path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    _write_json(paths_for(state_path)["kick"], {"at": time.time()})


def retry(key: str, state_path: Path | None = None) -> bool:
    p = paths_for(state_path)
    with _state_lock:
        st = load_state(p["state"])
        e = st["files"].get(key)
        if not e or e["status"] in ("processing", "queued"):
            return False
        e.update(status="queued", error="", retry=True)
        save_state(st, p["state"])
    return True


def rescan_now(state_path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    """List the watch folders into the state file (no processing)."""
    ap = Autopilot(state_path=state_path)
    cfg = ap.cfg()
    with _state_lock:
        st = ap._load()
        ap.rescan(cfg, st)
        ap._save(st)
    return api_state(state_path)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ title (no --title needed)
TITLE_BASES = [          # (publish theme, title) in priority order for "what was this session about"
    ("dragon", "I Fought the Ender Dragon"), ("nether", "I Went to the Nether in Minecraft"),
    ("dig", "I Dug Straight Down in Minecraft"), ("craft", "I Can't Even Craft in Minecraft"),
    ("build", "I Built a House in Minecraft"), ("diamonds", "I Found Diamonds in Minecraft"),
    ("creeper", "A Creeper Ruined My Minecraft Run"), ("mobs", "Mobs Ambushed Me in Minecraft"),
    ("lava", "Minecraft Lava Panic"), ("drown", "Minecraft Drowning Panic"), ("death", "I Died in Minecraft"),
    ("panic", "Minecraft Panic Moments"),
]
FALLBACK_TITLE = "Minecraft Funny Moments"


def derive_title(slug: str) -> str:
    """Heuristic title from the transcript (publish.py's keyword themes). Avoids words that switch the planner's mood
    (story / narrate / pov)."""
    from . import publish as PB
    tr = _read_json(PROJECTS / slug / "work" / "transcript.json", {}) or {}
    text = " ".join(s.get("text", "") for s in tr.get("segments", []))
    hits = {t: PB._hits(text, t) for t, _ in TITLE_BASES}
    best = max(hits.values()) if hits else 0
    if best <= 0:
        return FALLBACK_TITLE
    for theme, title in TITLE_BASES:
        if hits[theme] == best:
            return title
    return FALLBACK_TITLE


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ deliverables
def clean_name(s: str, n: int = 80) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r'[<>:"/\\|?*\x00-\x1f]', "", s).replace("…", "...").strip(" .")
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
    return (s[:n].rstrip(" .") or "Minecraft video")


def copy_paste_text(d: dict, shorts: list[dict], video_name: str) -> str:
    bar = "=" * 72

    def block(title: str, body: str) -> str:
        return f"{bar}\n{title}\n{bar}\n{body.strip()}\n"

    tags = d.get("tags") or []
    parts = [f"COPY-PASTE.txt for {video_name}\nEverything below is ready to paste into YouTube Studio / your "
             f"image generator. Generated automatically ({d.get('generator') or 'heuristic'}).\n"]
    parts.append(block("TITLE OPTIONS (pick one, 60 characters max)",
                       "\n".join(f"{i}. {t}" for i, t in enumerate(d.get("title_options") or [d.get("title", "")], 1))))
    parts.append(block("DESCRIPTION", d.get("description") or ""))
    parts.append(block(f"TAGS (paste as one line; {sum(len(t) for t in tags) + max(0, len(tags) - 1)} characters)",
                       ", ".join(tags)))
    parts.append(block("HASHTAGS", " ".join(d.get("hashtags") or [])))
    parts.append(block("THUMBNAIL TEXT OPTIONS", "\n".join(d.get("thumbnail_text_options") or [])))
    parts.append(block("THUMBNAIL PROMPT (with text)", d.get("thumbnail_prompt") or ""))
    parts.append(block("THUMBNAIL PROMPT (without text, add the words yourself)", d.get("thumbnail_prompt_no_text") or ""))
    parts.append(block("SHORTS COVER PROMPT (vertical 9:16)", d.get("shorts_cover_prompt") or ""))
    if d.get("warnings"):
        parts.append(block("HEADS UP", "\n".join(f"- {w}" for w in d["warnings"])))
    for i, s in enumerate(shorts, 1):
        parts.append(block(f"SHORT {i}: {s.get('file', '')}",
                           f"TITLE:\n{s.get('title', '')}\n\nDESCRIPTION:\n{s.get('description', '')}\n\n"
                           f"TAGS:\n{', '.join(s.get('tags') or [])}\n\nCOVER PROMPT:\n{s.get('cover_prompt', '')}"))
    return "\n".join(parts)


def deliver(slug: str, out_root: Path, dt: datetime, final: bool) -> dict:
    """Copy the finished video + Shorts and write COPY-PASTE.txt into <out_root>\\<YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM> <title>\\."""
    from . import publish as PB
    d = PB.load(slug)
    title = (d.get("title_options") or [d.get("title") or slug])[0]
    folder_name = f"{dt:%Y-%m-%d %H-%M} {clean_name(title, 70)}"
    out_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    folder, n = out_root / folder_name, 1
    while folder.exists() and (_read_json(folder / ".autopilot.json", {}) or {}).get("slug") != slug:
        n += 1
        folder = out_root / f"{folder_name} ({n})"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    _write_json(folder / ".autopilot.json", {"slug": slug})
    src = PROJECTS / slug / "out" / (f"{slug}.mp4" if final else f"{slug}_preview.mp4")
    if not src.exists():
        raise RuntimeError(f"rendered video not found: {src}")
    vname = clean_name(title) + ("" if final else " (preview 540p)") + ".mp4"
    shutil.copy2(src, folder / vname)
    shorts = []
    for i, s in enumerate(d.get("shorts") or [], 1):
        ssrc = PROJECTS / s["slug"] / "out" / (f"{s['slug']}.mp4" if final else f"{s['slug']}_preview.mp4")
        if not ssrc.exists():
            continue
        fname = f"Short {i} - {clean_name(re.sub(chr(35) + 'shorts', '', s.get('title', ''), flags=re.I), 50)}.mp4"
        shutil.copy2(ssrc, folder / fname)
        shorts.append({**s, "file": fname})
    (folder / "COPY-PASTE.txt").write_text(copy_paste_text(d, shorts, vname), encoding="utf-8-sig")
    return {"out_dir": str(folder), "title": title, "video": vname, "shorts": [s["file"] for s in shorts]}


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the worker (runs in its own low-priority process)
def _emit(tag: str, payload="") -> None:
    print(f"@@{tag} {payload}".rstrip(), flush=True)


def work(file: str, slug: str, out_root: str, shorts: bool, final: bool, replan: bool = False) -> dict:
    """The whole assembly line for one recording. Raises on failure (the parent records it)."""
    from . import publish as PB
    from .analyze import analyze
    from .autoplan import autoplan
    from .ingest import new_project
    from .render import render
    from .scaffold import scaffold
    from .settings import load as load_settings
    from .shorts import make_shorts
    from .transcribe import transcribe

    path = Path(file)
    proj = PROJECTS / slug
    warnings: list[str] = []
    t0 = time.time()
    info = probe_media(path)
    if not info:
        raise RuntimeError("not a readable video")
    tracks = choose_tracks(info["audio"])
    if not tracks:
        raise RuntimeError("no audio track")

    _emit("STAGE", "creating project")
    if not (proj / "project.json").exists():
        new_project(slug, str(path), None, tracks["mic_stream"], tracks["game_stream"], 0.0, None, False,
                    no_mic=tracks["mic_stream"] is None)
        pj = json.loads((proj / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        pj.update({"session": path.stem, "source_recording": str(path), "autopilot": {"tracks": tracks}})
        pj.setdefault("notes", []).append("autopilot: " + tracks["note"])
        (proj / "project.json").write_text(json.dumps(pj, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"[autopilot] audio: {tracks['note']}", flush=True)

    if not (proj / "work" / "transcript.json").exists():
        _emit("STAGE", "transcribing")
        transcribe(slug)
    if not (proj / "work" / "signals.json").exists():
        _emit("STAGE", "analyzing")
        analyze(slug)

    pj = json.loads((proj / "project.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if pj.get("title", slug) in (slug, "") or pj.get("title_auto"):
        pj["title"], pj["title_auto"] = derive_title(slug), True        # --title is not needed in this flow
        (proj / "project.json").write_text(json.dumps(pj, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"[autopilot] title: {pj['title']}", flush=True)

    edl_p = proj / "edit.json"
    planned = edl_p.exists() and json.loads(edl_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("generator") == "autoplan"
    if replan or not planned:
        _emit("STAGE", "planning the edit")
        try:
            scaffold(slug, force=edl_p.exists())
        except (SystemExit, Exception) as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - the scaffold is only a first draft
            warnings.append(f"scaffold skipped: {ex}")
        autoplan(slug)

    n_segs = len(json.loads(edl_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["segments"])
    _emit("STAGE", "rendering" if final else "rendering preview")
    segdir = proj / "work" / ("full" if final else "preview") / "segs"
    stop_poll = threading.Event()

    def poll_progress():
        last = -1
        while not stop_poll.wait(3):
            n = len(list(segdir.glob("*.mkv"))) if segdir.exists() else 0
            pct = min(90, int(90 * n / max(n_segs, 1)))
            if pct != last:
                _emit("PCT", pct)
                last = pct
    threading.Thread(target=poll_progress, daemon=True).start()
    try:
        render(slug, preview=not final, record=final)
    finally:
        stop_poll.set()
    _emit("PCT", 100)

    made: list[str] = []
    if shorts:
        sh = load_settings(slug)["shorts"]
        if sh["enabled"]:
            _emit("STAGE", "cutting Shorts")
            try:
                made = make_shorts(slug, render=False)
            except (SystemExit, Exception) as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
                warnings.append(f"shorts: {ex}")
            for k, s in enumerate(made, 1):
                _emit("STAGE", f"rendering Short {k}/{len(made)}")
                try:
                    render(s, preview=not final, record=False)
                except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - a failed Short must not lose the main video
                    warnings.append(f"{s}: render failed: {str(ex)[:200]}")
                    shutil.rmtree(PROJECTS / s, ignore_errors=True)
        else:
            warnings.append("Shorts are switched off in Settings > Shorts")

    _emit("STAGE", "writing title, description and tags")
    PB.generate(slug, use_llm=False)                                    # heuristic: no LLM, no network
    if final:
        PB.patch(slug, {"status": "rendered"})                          # Publishing board: Awaiting upload

    _emit("STAGE", "copying to the Finished folder")
    res = deliver(slug, Path(out_root), session_dt(path), final)
    res.update({"slug": slug, "warnings": warnings, "elapsed_s": round(time.time() - t0), "tracks": tracks["layout"]})
    _emit("RESULT", json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False))
    return res


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ CLI
def _print_status(state_path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    s = api_state(state_path)
    c = s["config"]
    print(f"autopilot: {'ON' if c['enabled'] else 'off'}  |  {s['status'].get('message', '')}")
    print(f"  watching : {'; '.join(c['watch_folders'])}")
    print(f"  finished : {c['output_folder']}")
    print(f"  runs     : {s['counts'] or 'none yet'}")
    for e in s["runs"][:15]:
        extra = e.get("out_dir") or e.get("error") or ""
        print(f"  {e['status']:<10} {e['name']:<28} {e.get('slug') or '':<28} {extra}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="mcs autopilot", description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True)
    for name in ("run", "once"):
        p = sub.add_parser(name)
        p.add_argument("--watch", action="append", help="watch folder (repeatable; default: settings)")
        p.add_argument("--output", help="Finished folder (default: settings)")
        p.add_argument("--min-length", type=float)
        p.add_argument("--max-age-h", type=float)
        p.add_argument("--no-wait-game", action="store_true", help="do not wait for Minecraft / OBS")
        p.add_argument("--no-shorts", action="store_true")
        p.add_argument("--preview-only", action="store_true", help="only a 540p preview")
        p.add_argument("--state-file", help="alternative state file (tests)")
        p.add_argument("--stable-s", type=float, help="seconds a file must be stable (default 30)")
    sub.add_parser("status")
    sub.add_parser("enable")
    sub.add_parser("disable")
    w = sub.add_parser("work", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    w.add_argument("--file", required=True)
    w.add_argument("--slug", required=True)
    w.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    w.add_argument("--shorts", dest="shorts", action="store_true", default=True)
    w.add_argument("--no-shorts", dest="shorts", action="store_false")
    w.add_argument("--final", dest="final", action="store_true", default=True)
    w.add_argument("--preview", dest="final", action="store_false")
    w.add_argument("--replan", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if a.action == "work":
        try:
            work(a.file, a.slug, a.out, a.shorts, a.final, a.replan)
        except BaseException as ex:  # noqa: BLE001 - report to the parent loop, which marks the file failed
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
            _emit("ERROR", f"{type(ex).__name__}: {ex}")
            sys.exit(1)
        return
    if a.action in ("enable", "disable"):
        from . import settings as SET
        SET.save_global({"autopilot": {"enabled": a.action == "enable"}})
        print(f"autopilot.enabled = {a.action == 'enable'}")
        return
    state_path = Path(a.state_file) if getattr(a, "state_file", None) else None
    if a.action == "status":
        _print_status(state_path)
        return
    ov = {"watch_folders": a.watch, "output_folder": a.output, "min_length_s": a.min_length,
          "max_age_h": a.max_age_h, "stable_s": a.stable_s}
    if a.no_wait_game:
        ov["wait_for_game"] = False
    if a.no_shorts:
        ov["make_shorts"] = False
    if a.preview_only:
        ov["render_final"] = False
    eng = Autopilot(ov, state_path)
    if a.action == "once":
        res = eng.once()
        _print_status(state_path)
        if "blocked" in res:
            print(f"[autopilot] stopped early: {eng.status_data.get('message')}")
        return
    try:
        eng.run_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        eng.request_stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Cinematic Director (replay B-roll)

You play normally while Flashback (and Replay Mod) record. Afterwards the editor works out where a cinematic shot helps the
video (an establishing aerial, an orbit after loot, a pull-back before a death, a chase cam in a panic...), asks the replay
for that shot, checks the clip, and lays it over the gameplay **while your voice keeps going**. The video never gets longer.

Code: `mcstudio/cinematic.py`. Tests: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe tests/test_cinematic.py` (or `mcs cinematic selftest`).

## The flow

```
OBS video + Flashback replay
  1 find_replay      pick the replay that overlaps the recording in wall-clock time
  2 sync             replay time at video t=0:  timestamps, then refined by motion cross-correlation
  3 plan_shots       choose shots from transcript beats, death screens, dark/calm stretches, replay events
                     -> projects/<slug>/broll/shots.json
  4 queue_jobs       studio/cinematic_jobs/<slug>/job-XX.json   (one per shot, with a Flashback editor state)
  5 exporter         fake | manual | flashback_auto  -> projects/<slug>/broll/<shot>.mp4
  6 qa_clip          reject black / frozen / blurred / inside-a-block / wrong-format clips (kept on disk, reason recorded)
  7 splice_into_edl  full-frame muted video overlays + a soft whoosh, only for rendered + QA-passed shots
```

CLI (run from `studio/`): `uv run mcs cinematic plan <slug>` (add `--synthetic` for a dry run without a replay),
`render <slug> [--exporter fake|manual|flashback_auto] [--force]`, `status <slug>`, `splice <slug>`
(writes `edit.json`, backup `edit.v_precinematic.json`), `qa <file> [--project slug]`, `sync <slug>`.

## Sync (how a shot finds its moment in the replay)

* OBS filename `YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS` is the recording start (whole seconds). It is refined to ~0.1 s with
  file end time minus the longest stream duration (real session: 36.92 s vs the OBS log's 36.83 s).
* Flashback `metadata.json` `name` is the **save time**, so start = name - total_ticks/20 (checked on the real files: the zip is
  written 2-5 s after `name`, and the Replay Mod recording of the same session ends within seconds of it).
* Replay Mod `metaData.json` `date` (epoch ms) is the **start**; `duration` is in ms.
* `estimate_sync` = video start - replay start (good to a second or two). `refine_sync` correlates the video's motion energy
  (ffmpeg, 4 fps, 64x36) with the replay player's speed + yaw rate + pitch rate over +-15 s and reports a confidence; below
  `sync_min_confidence` (0.4) it keeps the timestamp offset and says so.
* Measured on the real 15:02 session (94.5 s video): timestamps 22.6 s (filename only) / 23.5 s (refined start), motion
  cross-correlation 23.37 s, confidence 0.90. Run at 12 fps: 23.44 s overall, 23.47 s from the first half of the video and 23.41 s
  from the second half (independent estimates agree within 0.06 s, so no clock drift). The OBS log gives 23.43 s.

## Director rules (all configurable, see Settings > Cinematic shots)

* Plans on the **timeline the viewer sees**: output time when `edit.json` exists, else source time. A shot may run across a jump cut.
* 2.5-5 s per shot; at least `min_gap_s` (20) of normal footage between shots; at most `max_shots_per_min` (3) scaled by length
  (at least 1 for videos over 40 s); never the same kind back to back; first `hook_s` (8) seconds untouched.
* Never on a punchline word (beats of score 3+), a running-gag counter, a death screen, or an existing meme cutaway /
  green screen / sticker. Shots start just after the line lands.
* Intro `aerial_establish` at the first calm moment; loot/victory -> `orbit`/`push_in`; death -> `death_reveal` that **ends**
  just before the death screen; panic -> `track_follow`/`pov`; location/dimension -> `nether_arrival`; calm stretches ->
  `flyby`/`timelapse` (dark footage preferred); outro line -> `outro_pullup` (golden hour via time override for night sessions).
* When no window is free the shot is skipped and listed under `skipped` with the reason. A dense edit (lots of memes, counters and
  cuts) gets few shots: that is intended.
* Replay events (death, dimension, explosion, kill) are only trusted when sync confidence >= `trust_replay_events` (0.5).

## Contract: `projects/<slug>/broll/shots.json`

```jsonc
{"project": "ep01", "replay": "<zip>", "replay_kind": "flashback|replaymod|synthetic", "timeline": "output|source",
 "sync": {"offset_s": 23.37, "method": "timestamps|motion-xcorr|event", "confidence": 0.9, "notes": "..."},
 "settings": {"...snapshot of the cinematic settings..."},
 "notes": [], "skipped": [{"kind": "...", "reason": "...", "why": "..."}],
 "shots": [{
   "id": "shot-01", "kind": "aerial_establish|orbit|drone_pullup|push_in|flyby|track_follow|pov|spectate|timelapse|nether_arrival|death_reveal|outro_pullup",
   "moment": "intro|loot|death|panic|victory|travel|build|new_place|outro", "reason": "...",
   "video_t": 26.71,      // SOURCE second where the shot starts   (replay_tick = (video_t + offset_s) * 20)
   "out_t": 20.0,         // second on the planning timeline (output time when the plan was made from an edit)
   "replay_tick": 734, "ticks": 63, "dur_s": 3.15,
   "params": {"camera": {...abstract recipe...}, "anchor": {"tick","x","y","z","yaw","pitch"}|null,
              "visuals": {"hide_gui","hide_nametags","hide_chat","night_vision","time_of_day"}, "fps": 30},
   "status": "planned|queued|rendered|rejected|failed", "file": "broll/shot-01.mp4"|null, "qa": {...}|null}]}
```

Job file (`cinematic_jobs/<slug>/job-XX.json`): replay path, `tick_start/tick_end/ticks`, `anchor`, `camera.abstract`,
`camera.keyframes` (a validated Flashback editor state from `flashback_keyframes`, null if there is no replay), `visuals`,
`export` (1920x1080, fps 30 or 60 for POV, h264, `output` relative + `output_abs`).

## Splice

Each rendered, QA-passed shot becomes `{"type":"video","file":"broll/shot-01.mp4","placement":"fullscreen","audio":false,
"seg":<segment>,"src_at":<video_t>,"dur":<dur_s>,"cinematic":"shot-01"}` placed **under** stickers and motion graphics
(captions and text are drawn after overlays, so they stay readable), plus a quiet `whoosh` SFX (role `whoosh`, -2 dB nudge on
top of the automatic voice-relative level). Re-running removes and re-adds the cinematic items. Shots are dropped, not moved, if
they now overlap a meme/green screen/sticker, sit in the hook, or lose their footage. Vertical shorts leave the B-roll out.
`splice_into_edl(edl, slug)` is the pure function the autopilot calls.

## Real vs stubbed

| Piece | Status |
|---|---|
| Timestamp parsing, replay lookup, sync math, motion cross-correlation | real, verified on the real replays and a real OBS+Flashback session |
| Director, jobs, QA, splice, settings, CLI | real |
| Flashback editor states / keyframes | real (from `flashback_keyframes`, validated, not yet opened in the game) |
| `FakeExporter` | real: labelled placeholder clips for testing the pipeline |
| `ManualExporter` | real: writes `CHECKLIST.md`; export by hand into the given file, then run `render` again to QA it |
| `FlashbackAutoExporter` | **stub** (raises with a pointer to `docs/flashback-automation.md`) |
| Replay Mod `.mcpr` shots | windows/sync only; no reader, so no shots from `.mcpr` yet |
| Real shots in a real edit | not validated: needs the exporter plus a real OBS+Flashback session end to end |

def queue_jobs(slug: str, plan: dict | None = None, replay=None, retry_rejected: bool = False) -> list[Path]:
    """Write studio/cinematic_jobs/<slug>/job-XX.json for every shot still to render; marks them `queued`."""
    plan = plan or load_shots(slug)
    if not plan:
        raise SystemExit(f"{slug}: no shots.json - run: mcs cinematic plan {slug}")

    jd = job_dir(slug)
    jd.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = []
    redo = {"planned", "queued", "failed"} | ({"rejected"} if retry_rejected else set())
    for i, s in enumerate(plan["shots"], 1):
        if s["status"] not in redo:
            continue
        vis = s["params"]["visuals"]
        job = {"version": 1, "job_id": f"job-{i:02d}", "project": slug, "shot_id": s["id"], "kind": s["kind"],
               "replay": {"path": plan.get("replay"), "kind": plan.get("replay_kind")},
               "tick_start": s["replay_tick"], "ticks": s["ticks"],
               "tick_end": None if s["replay_tick"] is None else s["replay_tick"] + (
                   s["params"].get("replay_ticks_covered") or s["ticks"]),
               "dur_s": s["dur_s"], "anchor": s["params"].get("anchor"),
               "camera": {"abstract": s["params"]["camera"], "keyframes": _try_keyframes(s, replay)},
               "visuals": {"hide_gui": vis["hide_gui"], "hide_nametags": vis["hide_nametags"],
                           "hide_chat": vis["hide_chat"], "night_vision": vis["night_vision"],
                           "time_of_day_override": vis["time_of_day"]},
               "export": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": s["params"]["fps"], "codec": "h264",
                          "output": f"broll/{s['id']}.mp4",
                          "output_abs": str((PROJECTS / slug / "broll" / f"{s['id']}.mp4").resolve())},
               "status": "queued"}
        p = jd / f"{job['job_id']}.json"
        _write(p, job)
        s["status"], s["job"] = "queued", p.name
        out.append(p)
    _write(shots_path(slug), plan)
    return out

def _ff(args: list, timeout: int = 600) -> None:
    r = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-y", *map(str, args)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)

class FakeExporter(Exporter):
    """Placeholder clip: moving colour gradient + big text (kind, shot id, tick). Correct size / fps / duration, so the rest
    of the pipeline (QA, splice, render) can be exercised without Minecraft. job['fake_defect'] in
    {black, static, uniform} produces the matching bad clip for QA tests."""
    name = "fake"
    FONT = "C\\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf"

    def render(self, job: dict) -> Path:
        ex = job["export"]
        out = Path(ex["output_abs"])
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        w, h, fps, d = ex["width"], ex["height"], ex["fps"], job["dur_s"]
        c0, c1 = _KIND_COLORS.get(job["kind"], ("0x444444", "0xdddddd"))
        defect = job.get("fake_defect")
        lines = [job["kind"].upper().replace("_", " "), f"{job['shot_id']}   tick {job.get('tick_start')}",
                 f"{job['project']}  {d:.1f}s @ {fps}fps  [PLACEHOLDER]"]

        def txt(s, y, size):
            s = s.replace(":", "\\:")
            return (f"drawtext=fontfile='{self.FONT}':text='{s}':fontcolor=white:fontsize={size}:"
                    f"x=(w-text_w)/2:y={y}:borderw=4:bordercolor=black")
        label = ",".join([txt(lines[0], "h*0.30", 110), txt(lines[1], "h*0.46", 64), txt(lines[2], "h*0.58", 40)])
        mover = f"drawbox=x='mod(t*320,{w})':y=h*0.80:w=160:h=40:color=white@0.9:t=fill"
        if defect == "black":
            src = f"color=c=black:s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}"
            vf = "noise=alls=2:allf=t"
        elif defect == "static":
            src = f"color=c=0x3a7bd5:s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}"
            vf = txt(lines[0], "h*0.4", 100)
        elif defect == "uniform":
            src = f"color=c=0x6b4f2a:s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}"
            vf = f"noise=alls=3:allf=t,{mover}"
        else:
            src = f"gradients=s={w}x{h}:r={fps}:d={d}:c0={c0}:c1={c1}:speed=0.35:type=linear"
            vf = f"{mover},{label}"
        _ff(["-f", "lavfi", "-i", src, "-vf", vf + ",format=yuv420p", "-an", "-c:v", "libx264", "-preset", "veryfast",
             "-crf", "20", "-threads", "2", "-movflags", "+faststart", "-t", d, out])
        return out

        lines = md.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if md.exists() else [
            f"# Manual Flashback exports for {job['project']}", "",

            "keyframes described, tick Hide GUI / nametags / chat, export 1920x1080 H.264 to the given file.", ""]

                      f"- Replay: `{job['replay'].get('path')}`",
                      f"- Range: tick {job['tick_start']} to {job['tick_end']}  ({job['ticks']} ticks = {job['dur_s']:.1f}s)",
                      f"- Camera: {cam.get('move')} around the player; details `{json.dumps(cam)}`",
                      f"- Anchor (player at that tick): {job.get('anchor')}",

# =============================================================================================== render queue
def render_queue(slug: str, exporter: str | None = None, force: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Run the chosen exporter over queued jobs, QA each clip, update shots.json. Returns counts."""
    plan = load_shots(slug)
    if not plan:
        raise SystemExit(f"{slug}: no shots.json - run: mcs cinematic plan {slug}")
    C = cfg(SET.load(slug))
    name = exporter or C["exporter"]
    if name not in EXPORTERS:
        raise SystemExit(f"unknown exporter {name!r}; choose from {sorted(EXPORTERS)}")
    if C["render_only_when_idle"] and name != "manual" and not force and not machine_idle():
        print("[cinematic] Minecraft or OBS is running - not rendering now (settings: render_only_when_idle). "
              "Use --force to override.")
        return {"rendered": 0, "rejected": 0, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0, "deferred": True}
    exp = EXPORTERS[name]()
    ref = project_ref_luma(slug)
    counts = {"rendered": 0, "rejected": 0, "failed": 0, "waiting": 0}
    batched: dict[str, tuple[Path | None, str]] = {}          # shot id -> (clip, error)
    if hasattr(exp, "render_batch"):
        todo = [(s, _read(job_dir(slug) / (s.get("job") or "none.json"))) for s in plan["shots"]
                if s["status"] in ("queued", "failed")]
        todo = [(s, j) for s, j in todo if j]
        if todo:
            try:
                results = exp.render_batch([j for _, j in todo])
                by_out = {str(Path(r.output)): r for r in results if getattr(r, "output", None)}
                for sh, j in todo:
                    r = by_out.get(str(Path(j["export"]["output_abs"])))
                    if r is None:
                        batched[sh["id"]] = (None, "no result for this shot")
                    elif r.ok:
                        batched[sh["id"]] = (Path(r.output), "")
                    elif str(r.message).startswith("dry run"):
                        batched[sh["id"]] = (None, "")      # not rendered, nothing wrong -> 'waiting'
                    else:
                        batched[sh["id"]] = (None, str(r.message))
            except Exception as e:                           # noqa: BLE001 - one failure marks the whole batch
                for sh, _ in todo:
                    batched[sh["id"]] = (None, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    for s in plan["shots"]:
        if s["status"] not in ("queued", "failed"):
            continue
        job = _read(job_dir(slug) / (s.get("job") or "none.json"))
        if not job:
            s["status"], s["note"] = "failed", "job file missing - re-run queue"
            counts["failed"] += 1
            continue
        if s["id"] in batched:
            out, err = batched[s["id"]]
            if err:
                counts["failed"] += 1
                s["status"], s["note"] = "failed", err
                print(f"[cinematic] {s['id']} failed: {err}")
                continue
            if out is None:
                counts["waiting"] += 1
                continue
        else:
            out = None
        try:
            out = out if out is not None else exp.render(job)
        except NotImplementedError as e:
            print(f"[cinematic] {s['id']}: {e}")
            counts["failed"] += 1
            s["status"], s["note"] = "failed", str(e)
            continue
        except Exception as e:                                       # noqa: BLE001
            counts["failed"] += 1
            s["status"], s["note"] = "failed", f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
            print(f"[cinematic] {s['id']} failed: {s['note']}")
            continue
        if out is None:
            counts["waiting"] += 1
            continue
        ex = job["export"]
        qa = qa_clip(out, {"w": ex["width"], "h": ex["height"], "fps": ex["fps"], "dur": job["dur_s"]}, ref)
        s["file"], s["qa"] = ex["output"], qa
        s["status"] = "rendered" if qa["ok"] else "rejected"
        s.pop("note", None)
        if not qa["ok"]:
            s["note"] = "; ".join(qa["reasons"])
        counts[s["status"]] += 1
        print(f"[cinematic] {s['id']} {s['kind']:<16} {s['status']}" + ("" if qa["ok"] else f"  ({s['note']})"))
        _write(shots_path(slug), plan)
    _write(shots_path(slug), plan)
    if name == "manual" and counts["waiting"]:
        print(f"[cinematic] checklist written: {job_dir(slug) / 'CHECKLIST.md'}")
    return counts

def _whoosh(slug: str, seed: int = 1) -> str | None:
    try:
        from . import assets as A
        res = A.find(A.Query(roles=["whoosh"], max_duration=1.6, max_energy=3, project=slug, limit=4, seed=seed))
        return res[0]["id"] if res else None
    except Exception:                                                # noqa: BLE001

def splice(edl: dict, slug: str, S: dict | None = None) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """Add rendered + QA-passed shots as full-frame muted `video` overlays (and a soft whoosh). Returns (edl, report).
    Idempotent: earlier cinematic overlays/sfx are removed first. No usable shots -> the edl comes back unchanged."""
    S = S if S is not None else SET.load(slug)
    C = cfg(S)
    report: dict = {"added": [], "skipped": []}
    plan = load_shots(slug)
    if not plan or not C["enabled"]:
        report["note"] = "cinematic disabled" if plan else "no shots.json"
        return edl, report
    out = copy.deepcopy(edl)
    out["overlays"] = [o for o in out.get("overlays", []) if not o.get("cinematic")]
    out.setdefault("audio", {}).setdefault("sfx", [])
    out["audio"]["sfx"] = [e for e in out["audio"]["sfx"] if not e.get("cinematic")]
    usable = [s for s in plan["shots"] if s["status"] == "rendered" and (s.get("qa") or {}).get("ok", True)
              and s["kind"] in C["allowed_kinds"] and s.get("file")]
    if not usable:
        report["note"] = "no rendered shots"
        return out, report
    from . import assets as A
    from .edl import build_spans, validate

    def look(i):
        try:
            return A.get(i)
        except Exception:                                            # noqa: BLE001
            return None
    spans = build_spans(out, look)
    busy = busy_output_intervals(out, spans, pad=0.3)
    total_out = max(sp.out_end for sp in spans)
    sfx_on = S.get("audio", {}).get("sfx", True) and SET.role_ok(S, ["whoosh"]) and C["whoosh"]
    who = _whoosh(slug) if sfx_on else None
    placed: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
    new_ov, new_sfx = [], []
    for sh in sorted(usable, key=lambda s: s["video_t"]):
        if not (PROJECTS / slug / sh["file"]).exists():
            report["skipped"].append({"id": sh["id"], "why": "clip file missing"})
            continue
        dur = sh["dur_s"]
        cover = [sp for sp in spans if sp.src_in is not None and not str(sp.seg_id or "").startswith("cold")
                 and (sp.speed == 1.0 or sh["kind"] == "timelapse")
                 and sp.src_in - 0.01 <= sh["video_t"] < sp.src_in + (sp.out_end - sp.out_start) * sp.speed]
        if not cover:
            report["skipped"].append({"id": sh["id"], "why": "that footage was cut from the edit"})
            continue
        sp = cover[0]
        src_at = sh["video_t"]               # the overlay starts on this footage; it may run on across a jump cut
        o0 = sp.out_start + (src_at - sp.src_in) / sp.speed
        o1 = o0 + dur
        if o1 > total_out + 1e-6:
            report["skipped"].append({"id": sh["id"], "why": "would run past the end of the video"})
            continue
        if o0 < C["hook_s"]:
            report["skipped"].append({"id": sh["id"], "why": f"inside the hook (first {C['hook_s']:g}s)"})
            continue
        clash = next((w for a, z, w in busy if o0 < z and o1 > a), None)
        if clash:
            report["skipped"].append({"id": sh["id"], "why": f"overlaps {clash}"})
            continue
        if any(not (o0 >= b1 + C["min_gap_s"] or o1 + C["min_gap_s"] <= b0) for b0, b1 in placed):
            report["skipped"].append({"id": sh["id"], "why": "too close to another shot"})
            continue
        placed.append((o0, o1))
        new_ov.append({"type": "video", "file": sh["file"], "placement": "fullscreen", "audio": False,
                       "seg": sp.seg_id, "src_at": round(src_at, 3), "dur": dur, "cinematic": sh["id"],
                       "kind": sh["kind"]})
        if who:
            new_sfx.append({"asset": who, "seg": sp.seg_id, "src_at": round(src_at + 0.05, 3), "align": "peak",
                            "volume_db": -2, "cinematic": sh["id"]})
        report["added"].append({"id": sh["id"], "kind": sh["kind"], "out_at": round(o0, 2), "seg": sp.seg_id})
    out["overlays"] = new_ov + out["overlays"]          # underneath stickers / motion graphics / avatar, above the footage
    out["audio"]["sfx"] = out["audio"]["sfx"] + new_sfx
    validate(out)
    if not report["added"]:
        return edl, report
    return out, report


def splice_into_edl(edl: dict, slug: str) -> dict:
    """Pure function used by autopilot: the edl with cinematic B-roll overlays added (unchanged if there is none)."""
    try:
        return splice(edl, slug)[0]
    except Exception as e:                                           # noqa: BLE001 - B-roll must never break an edit
        print(f"[cinematic] splice skipped: {type(e).__name__}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return edl

def status_text(slug: str) -> str:

        return f"{slug}: no shots.json yet (mcs cinematic plan {slug})"
    sy = p["sync"]
    lines = [f"{slug}: replay {p.get('replay') or '-'} ({p.get('replay_kind')})",
             f"  sync {sy['offset_s']:+.2f}s via {sy['method']} conf {sy['confidence']} - {sy['notes']}"]
    c: dict = {}
    for s in p["shots"]:
        lines.append(f"  {s['id']} {s['video_t']:>7.2f}s {s['kind']:<16} {s['status']:<9} {s.get('file') or '-'}"
                     + (f"  [{s['note']}]" if s.get("note") else ""))
        c[s["status"]] = c.get(s["status"], 0) + 1
    lines.append("  totals: " + (", ".join(f"{v} {k}" for k, v in sorted(c.items())) or "no shots"))
    return "\n".join(lines)

import threading

from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from mcstudio import flashback_export as FE  # noqa: E402

L = FE.launcher()
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="fa_test_"))
passed: list[str] = []


def ok(msg: str):
    passed.append(msg)
    print("  ok -", msg)


def make_replay(name="replay.zip") -> Path:
    p = tmp / name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(p, "w") as z:
        z.writestr("metadata.json", json.dumps({"uuid": "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555", "total_ticks": 3000}))
    return p


def make_job(folder: Path, n=2, replay: Path | None = None, **over) -> Path:
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    replay = replay or make_replay()
    jobs = []
    for i in range(n):
        j = {"scene": i, "name": f"{i:02d}_orbit", "start": 100 + i * 200, "end": 220 + i * 200,
             "output": str(folder / "out" / f"{i:02d}_orbit.mp4"), "width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": 60.0,
             "container": "MP4", "codec": "H264", "encoder": None, "bitrate": 20000000, "ssaa": False, "noGui": True,
             "resetRng": False, "recordAudio": False, "transparent": False, "kind": "orbit", "note": ""}
        j.update(over)
        jobs.append(j)
    p = folder / "jobs.json"
    p.write_text(json.dumps({"version": 1, "replay": str(replay), "jobs": jobs}), encoding="utf-8")
    return p


def expect_job_error(data, what):
    p = tmp / "bad_jobs.json"
    p.write_text(json.dumps(data) if not isinstance(data, str) else data, encoding="utf-8")

        FE.parse_jobs(p)

        return
    raise AssertionError(f"should reject: {what}")


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ fakes
class FakeProc:
    """Stands in for the Minecraft process. `script(job_path, proc)` runs in a thread and plays the mod's role."""
    def __init__(self, job_path, script=None, exit_after_script=True):
        self.pid = 4242
        self.job = Path(job_path)
        self.killed = False
        self.rc = None
        self._done = threading.Event()
        self.exit_after_script = exit_after_script
        self.t = threading.Thread(target=self._run, args=(script,), daemon=True)
        if script:
            self.t.start()

    def _run(self, script):
        try:
            script(self.job, self)
        finally:
            if self.exit_after_script and self.rc is None and not self.killed:
                self.rc = 0

    def poll(self):
        return self.rc

    def kill_tree(self):
        self.killed = True
        self.rc = 1


def write_status(job: Path, **kw):
    st = {"modVersion": "0.1.0", "state": "starting", "message": "", "pid": 1, "updatedMs": int(time.time() * 1000),
          "jobIndex": -1, "jobCount": 0, "job": None, "progressPct": 0, "frames": 0, "totalFrames": 0, "results": [], "errors": []}
    if "current" in kw:
        kw["job"] = kw.pop("current")
    st.update(kw)
    tmpf = job.with_name("status.json.tmp")
    tmpf.write_text(json.dumps(st), encoding="utf-8")
    for _ in range(50):                      # Windows: replace fails while the monitor has the file open; the mod just retries next tick
        try:
            tmpf.replace(job.with_name("status.json"))
            return
        except PermissionError:
            time.sleep(0.01)


def good_script(job: Path, proc: FakeProc):
    jf = FE.parse_jobs(job)
    results = []
    write_status(job, state="starting", jobCount=len(jf.shots))
    time.sleep(0.15)
    write_status(job, state="opening", jobCount=len(jf.shots))
    time.sleep(0.15)
    for i, s in enumerate(jf.shots):
        write_status(job, state="exporting", jobIndex=i, jobCount=len(jf.shots), current=s["name"], progressPct=50, results=results)
        time.sleep(0.15)
        out = Path(s["output"])
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_bytes(b"x" * 1000)
        results.append({"index": i, "name": s["name"], "scene": s["scene"], "output": str(out), "ok": True, "bytes": 1000,
                        "frames": 120, "durationS": 2.0, "wallS": 5.0, "message": ""})
    write_status(job, state="done", jobIndex=len(jf.shots) - 1, jobCount=len(jf.shots), progressPct=100, results=results)

def xcorr_offset(v: np.ndarray, r: np.ndarray, fps: float, prior_s: float = 0.0, max_lag_s: float = 15.0,
                 min_overlap_s: float = 10.0, smooth_s: float = 1.0) -> dict:
    """Find offset o (replay time at video t0) maximising Pearson correlation of v[k] with r[k + o*fps].
    Search prior +- max_lag. confidence in 0..1 combines the peak height and its prominence over the best
    rival peak further than 1.5 s away. Returns {offset_s, confidence, peak, second, n}."""
    sm = max(1, int(round(smooth_s * fps)))
    v = _z(_smooth(np.asarray(v, float), sm))
    r = _z(_smooth(np.asarray(r, float), sm))
    lo, hi = int(round((prior_s - max_lag_s) * fps)), int(round((prior_s + max_lag_s) * fps))
    min_n = int(min_overlap_s * fps)
    shifts, cors = [], []
    for s in range(lo, hi + 1):
        k0, k1 = max(0, -s), min(len(v), len(r) - s)
        if k1 - k0 < min_n:
            continue
        a, b = v[k0:k1], r[k0 + s:k1 + s]
        sa, sb = a.std(), b.std()
        if sa < 1e-9 or sb < 1e-9:
            continue
        shifts.append(s)
        cors.append(float(np.mean((a - a.mean()) * (b - b.mean())) / (sa * sb)))
    if not shifts:
        return {"offset_s": prior_s, "confidence": 0.0, "peak": 0.0, "second": 0.0, "n": 0}
    cors_a = np.array(cors)
    i = int(np.argmax(cors_a))
    peak = cors_a[i]
    far = np.abs(np.array(shifts) - shifts[i]) > 1.5 * fps
    second = float(cors_a[far].max()) if far.any() else 0.0
    frac = 0.0                                              # parabolic sub-sample refinement
    if 0 < i < len(cors_a) - 1:
        a, b, c = cors_a[i - 1], cors_a[i], cors_a[i + 1]
        den = a - 2 * b + c
        frac = 0.5 * (a - c) / den if abs(den) > 1e-9 else 0.0
        frac = max(-1.0, min(1.0, frac))
    conf = max(0.0, min(1.0, (peak - 0.2) / 0.5)) * max(0.0, min(1.0, (peak - second) / 0.2))
    return {"offset_s": (shifts[i] + frac) / fps, "confidence": round(float(conf), 3), "peak": round(float(peak), 3),
            "second": round(second, 3), "n": len(shifts)}


def refine_sync(video_path: str | Path | None, replay, est: dict, min_conf: float = 0.4, fps: float = 4.0,
                max_lag_s: float = 15.0, v_series: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict:
    """Refine a timestamp estimate by cross-correlating video motion energy with the replay's player speed / yaw-rate.
    Falls back to the timestamp estimate (with a note) when the correlation is weak or inputs are missing."""
    try:
        r_series = replay_activity(replay.player_track(), fps)
        v = v_series if v_series is not None else video_motion_series(video_path, fps)
    except Exception as e:                                   # noqa: BLE001 - never block planning on sync refinement
        return {**est, "notes": est["notes"] + f"; xcorr skipped ({type(e).__name__}: {e})"}
    if len(v) < 10 * fps:
        return {**est, "notes": est["notes"] + "; xcorr skipped (video too short)"}
    res = xcorr_offset(v, r_series, fps, est["offset_s"], max_lag_s)
    if res["confidence"] >= min_conf:
        return {"offset_s": round(res["offset_s"], 3), "method": "motion-xcorr", "confidence": res["confidence"],
                "notes": f"xcorr peak r={res['peak']} (rival {res['second']}); timestamp guess was "
                         f"{est['offset_s']:+.2f}s, refined shift {res['offset_s'] - est['offset_s']:+.2f}s"}
    return {**est, "notes": est["notes"] + f"; xcorr too weak (conf {res['confidence']}, r={res['peak']}) - "
                                           "kept the timestamp offset"}


# =============================================================================================== replay access
@dataclass
class SynthTrack:
def load_replay(path: str | Path):
    """flashback_replay.load(path) (Flashback only; Replay Mod .mcpr has no reader yet)."""
    if str(path).lower().endswith(".mcpr"):
        raise NotImplementedError("Replay Mod (.mcpr) shots need a reader; only Flashback replays are supported so far")
    from . import flashback_replay as F
    return F.load(path)

def _words(tr: dict) -> list[dict]:
"""Cinematic Director: replay-powered B-roll (aerials, orbits, POV, spectate...) spliced into the edit automatically.

While Flashback (or Replay Mod) records, the creator just plays. This module turns that replay into shots:

    find_replay(slug)        which replay overlaps the OBS recording in wall-clock time

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ [autopilot-cinematic] the cinematic-shots step
CINEMATIC_MESSAGES = {      # stage -> live status line on the Autopilot page
    "cinematic shots: planning": "Planning cinematic shots from the replay…",
    "cinematic shots: waiting": "Waiting for Minecraft to close before rendering cinematic shots…",
    "cinematic shots: rendering": "Rendering cinematic shots… Minecraft will open for a minute or two: please leave "
                                  "the PC alone",
    "cinematic shots: splicing": "Adding the cinematic shots to the edit…",
}
CINEMATIC_EXPORTER_FACTORY = None      # tests only: callable(holder: list) -> exporter object (a test double)
CINEMATIC_POLL_S = 10.0                # how often the step re-checks "is Minecraft still open"
CINEMATIC_KILL_GRACE_S = 90.0          # after the watchdog kills the game: how long the exporter may take to clean up


def _empty_cinematic() -> dict:
    return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "", "shots": {"planned": 0, "rendered": 0, "rejected": 0, "failed": 0},
            "replay": None, "sync_offset_s": None, "sync_confidence": None, "spliced": 0}


def _real_cinematic_exporter(holder: list):
    """The real thing: FlashbackAutoExporter(launch=True). `spawn` only remembers the game process so the watchdog can
    kill its whole tree; it launches exactly what the exporter would have launched."""
    from .flashback_export import FlashbackAutoExporter, launcher

    def spawn(plan, log):
        proc = launcher().launch(plan, log)
        holder.append(proc)
        return proc
    return FlashbackAutoExporter(launch=True, spawn=spawn)


def _cinematic_cleanup(slug: str, mc_dir=None) -> list[str]:
    """Belt and braces after ANY failed/aborted export (the exporter already does this in its `finally`; this makes it
    true even if the exporter itself was cut short): remove ARMED markers of this project's runs and put back the
    creator's flashback editor states. Idempotent, never raises."""
    done: list[str] = []
    try:
        from .flashback_export import JOBS_DIR, MC_DIR, launcher
        for job in (JOBS_DIR / slug).glob("run-*/jobs.json"):
            if job.with_name("ARMED").exists():
                launcher().disarm(job)
                done.append(f"disarmed {job.parent.name}")
        ed = Path(mc_dir or MC_DIR) / "flashback" / "editor_states"
        for bak in ed.glob("*.json.flashback_auto_backup"):
            target = bak.with_name(bak.name[: -len(".flashback_auto_backup")])
            shutil.copy2(bak, target)
            bak.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            done.append(f"restored {target.name}")
    except Exception as ex:  # noqa: BLE001
        done.append(f"cleanup error: {type(ex).__name__}: {ex}")
    return done


def _strip_cinematic(edl: dict) -> dict:
    out = json.loads(json.dumps(edl))
    out["overlays"] = [o for o in out.get("overlays", []) if not o.get("cinematic")]
    sfx = (out.get("audio") or {}).get("sfx")
    if sfx is not None:
        out["audio"]["sfx"] = [x for x in sfx if not x.get("cinematic")]
    return out


def _count_shots(plan: dict | None) -> dict:
    c = {"planned": 0, "rendered": 0, "rejected": 0, "failed": 0}
    for sh in (plan or {}).get("shots", []):
        c["planned"] += 1
        if sh.get("status") in ("rendered", "rejected", "failed"):
            c[sh["status"]] += 1
    return c


def cinematic_step(slug: str, replan: bool = False, factory=None, emit=None, wait_cfg: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """find_replay -> plan_shots (sync) -> queue_jobs -> render_queue (REAL exporter, game launched headlessly) -> QA ->
